pages.text: A ribosome reads about 10 codons a second and gets about one in ten thousand wrong. Read faster and it errs more, ε = 10⁻⁴·e^((v − 10)/8); magnesium away from 10 mM loosens it. A chain of L codons is right only if every codon is: (1 − ε)^L.
$(thing)Set$(): Reading speed, Magnesium.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Wobbling tRNA: the error varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Faster reading is faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Errors per codon: ε = 10⁻⁴·e^((v − 10)/8)·(1 + ((Mg − 10)/8)²)$(br)Chains right: Y = (1 − ε)^L
